title: Demand Service Rate Programs: The Window a Ceiling Review Reads
content:
**Where the program has run less than a full term and dispatch privileges have been restored during
it**, the record is read from the day they were restored, counting each month or part month up to the
day of the review.

**Where the program has run less than a full term and privileges have not been restored during it**, the
record is read from the day the current term started, counting each month or part month up to the day of
the review.

**In any other case** neither term above shortens the window the record is read over.

Whether the program has run less than a full term is judged by the months run since the current term
started against the term length published for the program the account holds under the Demand Service Rate Programs:

| Program | Term (calendar months) |
|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 12 |
| Priority Response Program | 12 |
| Block Hour Service Program | 12 |
| Emergency Response Program | 12 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 24 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 24 |

| Months run since the current term started | Dispatch privileges restored during the term | The window read |
|---|---|---|
| fewer than the tier's term length | yes | from the day they were restored to the day of the review, each month or part month counted |
| fewer than the tier's term length | no | from the day the current term started to the day of the review, each month or part month counted |
| the tier's term length or more | either | neither term above shortens the window |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** On the Priority Response Program, whose term is 12 calendar months, a
program 5 months into its term on which privileges were restored 2 months ago has its record read over
those 2 months and the part month up to the day of the review, which is 3 months; had privileges never
been withdrawn, the record would be read from the term start, which is 6 months counting the part month.
